scope: Make DRW_Hatch DWG encoding transactional across caller body, string, and handle buffers, and verify allocation-failure rollback plus same-object retry.

changes: Run HATCH encoding through encodeEntityDwgTransaction so mutations to output buffers and oType are committed only after successful encoding.
Route body, string, and handle writes through the transaction-provided staged buffers while preserving existing alias behavior and fallback of strings to the body buffer.
implementation.failureBehavior: Injected allocation failure leaves caller buffer bytes and bit positions, plus oType, unchanged; retrying the same entity against the same buffers reproduces the clean successful encoding.

validation.focusedTestResult: PASS: 548 allocation offsets across 6 DWG versions and 30 version/stream-layout profiles

coverage: DWG writer versions AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032.
Five stream alias layouts per version: distinct streams, shared string/handle stream, body/string alias, body/handle alias, and all streams aliased.
Allocation failure at each exercised allocation point verifies byte/bit-position and oType rollback followed by successful same-object, same-buffer retry and exact comparison to clean output.
Generated associative patterned HATCH includes seed points and a line boundary with a boundary handle.
limitations: Generated allocation and retry controls establish transaction behavior only; they do not qualify physical DWG producer profiles, HATCH semantic fidelity, or native consumer acceptance.
No DWG or DXF drawing fixture was added.
